Axis scalings

Source: R/graph_scale.R
graph_scale.Rd

Scales control how values along a NumberLine() or the axes of a coordinate system map to positions. LinearBase() multiplies values by a constant; LogBase() turns the axis into a logarithmic one, so that an axis with x_range = c(-1, 3) spans 10^-1 to 10^3.

Usage

LinearBase(scale_factor = 1)

LogBase(base = 10, custom_labels = TRUE)

Arguments

scale_factor

The slope of the linear scaling.

base

The base of the logarithm.

custom_labels

Whether axes using this scale build their own labels (with Integer()) instead of plain decimal numbers.

Value

A scale object.

Details

Each scale has the methods func(value) (the scaling itself, called function upstream, which is a reserved word in R) and inverse_function(value). LogBase also has get_custom_labels(val_range, unit_decimal_places = 0, ...), which returns Integer() labels of the form \(10^{k}\).

Examples

LogBase(base = 2)$func(3)
#> [1] 8
LinearBase(2)$inverse_function(4)
#> [1] 2
